Hab 3:7 Vulgate 'Æthiópiæ' corresponds to Hebrew Cushan; 思高 uses '雇商' (Cushan) not Ethiopia — retained 思高 rendering. 3. Hab 3:8 Vulgate 'furor tuus' (your fury toward rivers) is split between the two river clauses in the Latin; rendered to match Vulgate's three-part structure while using 思高-style wording. 4. Jer 14:17 思高 v.17 opens with a narrative frame ('你应将这话转告他们：'); the breviary canticum starts from the first-person lament proper, so translated from '我眼泪' onward, consistent with Vulgate sense. 5.
